response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT s.riskeval AS riskeval, SUM(c.gbsize) * 1.0 / SUM(c.spanmin) AS rate FROM scans c JOIN sites s ON c.zoneref = s.zoneregistry GROUP BY s.riskeval), b AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS bench FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.rate) AS avg_rate_above_benchmark, AVG(g.rate - b.bench) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.rate > b.bench

assumptions.assumption: Scans whose site has no recorded risk evaluation status are those with a NULL riskeval; GROUP BY puts all NULLs into one group. Empty strings are not treated as missing.
A group whose total spanmin is 0 or NULL has a NULL rate (SQLite division by zero gives NULL). Such a group is ignored in the benchmark average and can never be strictly above it.
If no group exceeds the benchmark, or there is no benchmark, the query still returns one row with NULL in both columns.
